faq.a: A mother lode is the main vein of ore, usually gold or silver, from which smaller deposits branch off. Figuratively, it means a rich source or an abundant supply of something valuable.

faq.q: Is it mother lode or mother load?
faq.a: Mother lode is the standard spelling, because it comes from the mining word 'lode.' Mother load is a common misspelling, sometimes used on purpose as a pun.

faq.q: What does 'hit the mother lode' mean?
faq.a: It means to discover a large supply of something you want or to have a major breakthrough. You might hit the mother lode of bargains, ideas, or opportunities.

faq.q: Where does the phrase mother lode come from?
faq.a: It comes from mining, where it described the primary vein of ore. In California, the Mother Lode became the name of a gold-bearing belt in the Sierra Nevada foothills during the Gold Rush.
A lode is a vein of metal ore running through rock. The mother lode is the largest or principal vein in an area.

faq.q: How can I find my own mother lode in life?
faq.a: Follow small signs of energy and interest, look closely at what you already have, and keep going longer than feels comfortable. Most breakthroughs come after patient, steady effort.
